```yaml
# Context Adaptations — slides-creator
# Extracted from McKinsey PPT Architect "ADAPTAÇÕES POR CONTEXTO"
# Executable lookup: normalize-briefing + write-action-titles + create-presentation consume this

schema_version: "1.0"
name: context-adaptations
owner_squad: slides-creator
source: "docs/squad/slides/enterprise_slides/output/mckinsey_ppt_architect_instructions.md#ADAPTAÇÕES POR CONTEXTO"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# LANGUAGE ADAPTATIONS (lookup by briefing.normalized.language)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
language:
  pt-BR:
    default: true
    title_case: sentence_case  # "Market share caiu 15% em 2023"
    number_format:
      thousands_separator: "."
      decimal_separator: ","
      example: "1.234,56"
    date_format_short: "DD/MM/AAAA"
    date_format_long: "15 de dezembro de 2024"
    apa_style: "APA latino-americano"

  en:
    title_case: title_case  # "Market Share Declined by 15% in 2023"
    number_format:
      thousands_separator: ","
      decimal_separator: "."
      example: "1,234.56"
    date_format_short: "MM/DD/YYYY"
    date_format_long: "December 15, 2024"
    apa_style: "APA americano"

  es:
    title_case: sentence_case
    number_format:
      thousands_separator: "."
      decimal_separator: ","
      example: "1.234,56"
    date_format_short: "DD/MM/AAAA"
    date_format_long: "15 de diciembre de 2024"
    apa_style: "APA latino-americano"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CULTURAL ADAPTATIONS (lookup by briefing.normalized.audience.culture)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
culture:
  asia_east:  # China, Japão, Coreia
    formality_level: high
    initial_slides: "more_formal"
    density_tolerance: high
    color_semantics:
      red: "luck/prosperity (positive)"
      white: "mourning in some contexts (use cautiously)"
    number_semantics:
      "8": auspicious
      "4": avoided (death association)
    narrative_style: hierarchy_respecting

  middle_east:
    formality_level: high
    opulence: "moderate_acceptable (gold, premium materials positive)"
    human_representation: "consider_abstraction (avoid detailed faces in some contexts)"
    reading_direction_arabic: "right_to_left (if applicable)"
    narrative_style: relationship_first

  latam:
    formality_level: moderate
    warmth: high
    color_palette: "vibrant_colors_acceptable"
    narrative_style: "more_contextual (expect_narrative_buildup)"
    density_tolerance: moderate

  europe_north:  # Escandinávia, UK, Alemanha, Holanda
    formality_level: moderate
    minimalism: "high (less_is_more)"
    sustainability_esg: "mention_valued"
    narrative_style: "direct (less_emotional_storytelling, high_efficiency)"
    density_tolerance: low

  us:
    formality_level: moderate
    storytelling: "high (hero_journey_structures_work)"
    data_density: moderate
    narrative_style: "insight_first + proof"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# AUDIENCE ADAPTATIONS (lookup by briefing.normalized.audience.role)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
audience:
  c_level:
    slide_count_target: "max 15-20 for 30min"
    density: low  # 1-2 key points per slide
    data_depth: "high-level + strategic implications"
    action_titles: "insight + magnitude + implied_action"
    appendix_usage: "move details to appendix"

  board:
    slide_count_target: "max 10-15 for 30min"
    density: very_low  # 1 key point per slide
    data_depth: "executive_summary_quality"
    action_titles: "decision_oriented"
    approval_markers: "explicit_decisions_requested slides"

  strategy_team:
    slide_count_target: "20-40"
    density: moderate  # 2-3 key points per slide
    data_depth: "analytical_depth + methodology"
    action_titles: "analytical + framework_based"

  operators:
    slide_count_target: "15-30"
    density: moderate_to_high
    data_depth: "process_depth + operational_detail"
    action_titles: "action_oriented + operational"

  investors:
    slide_count_target: "15-25"
    density: low
    data_depth: "financial_rigor + market_context"
    action_titles: "value_creation_oriented"
    required_sections: [problem, solution, market, traction, team, ask]

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CONSUMER TASKS
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
consumers:
  - task: normalize-briefing
    purpose: "Extract audience.culture + audience.role + language from briefing; apply defaults"
  - task: write-action-titles
    purpose: "Apply title_case rule by language"
  - task: create-presentation
    purpose: "Apply number/date format by language across all slides"
  - task: validate-fontes-apa
    purpose: "Apply APA style per language rule"
  - task: compose-grid-layout
    purpose: "Adjust density + whitespace by audience.role"

meta:
  absorbed_from: "mckinsey_ppt_architect_instructions.md lines 1435-1487"
  absorbed_date: "2026-04-21"
```


## Referência: references/squad/data/cost-tracking.yaml

```yaml
# Cost Tracking & Budget Guardrails Configuration
# SSOT for cost monitoring, budget enforcement, and circuit breaker logic.
# Consumed by: visual-scout (pre-call check), slide-chief (budget reporting),
#               qa-inspector (cost validation per deck).
# Created by: Story 1.4 (EPIC-SC-V2-001, Sprint 1)
# Dependency: visual-engines.yaml (estimateCost per engine, orchestration.budget_cap_*)

cost_tracking:
  version: "1.0.0"
  created_at: "2026-03-20"
  epic: EPIC-SC-V2-001
  story: "1.4"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # BUDGET CAPS (hard limits -- pipeline halts when reached)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  budget_caps:
    per_deck:
      env_var: SLIDES_COST_CAP
      default_usd: 2.00
      description: >
        Maximum total cost for visual generation in a single deck.
        When reached, only free engines (d2, mermaid, plotly) are allowed.
        Paid engines (gpt_image, recraft, ideogram) are skipped with
        VisualError(type=engine_failure, message="deck budget exceeded").
      enforcement: hard
      action_on_breach: block_paid_engines

    per_video:
      env_var: SLIDES_VIDEO_COST_CAP
      default_usd: 5.00
      description: >
        Maximum total cost for video-related processing per video input.
        Applies to YouTube-to-Presentation pipeline (Story 4.x).
        When reached, pipeline continues with already-processed frames.
      enforcement: hard
      action_on_breach: block_paid_engines

    monthly:
      env_var: SLIDES_MONTHLY_BUDGET
      default_usd: 100.00
      description: >
        Monthly budget ceiling. Not a hard block -- triggers warning at
        threshold and logs to console. Operator can override via env var.
      enforcement: soft
      action_on_breach: warn_and_log

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # WARNING THRESHOLDS
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  warning_thresholds:
    monthly_budget_warning_pct: 80
    description: >
      When monthly accumulated cost exceeds this percentage of
      SLIDES_MONTHLY_BUDGET, emit a console warning with current spend
      and remaining budget. Warning repeats every 10% increment after.
    warning_format: >
      [SLIDES-COST-WARNING] Monthly spend: ${current_usd} / ${budget_usd}
      (${pct}%). Remaining: ${remaining_usd}. Consider reviewing engine usage.

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # PRE-CALL COST CHECK (estimateCost guard)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  pre_call_check:
    description: >
      Before every paid API call, visual-scout MUST:
      1. Call estimateCost(spec) on the target engine
      2. Compare estimated cost against remaining deck budget
      3. If estimate > remaining: skip engine, try next in fallback chain
      4. If all paid engines exceed budget: use free engines only
    algorithm:
      steps:
        - "1. remaining = budget_cap_per_deck - deck_accumulated_cost"
        - "2. estimate = engine.estimateCost(spec).amount_usd"
        - "3. IF estimate > remaining THEN skip engine, log reason"
        - "4. IF estimate <= remaining THEN proceed with render()"
        - "5. After render: actual_cost = output.metadata.cost_usd"
        - "6. deck_accumulated_cost += actual_cost"
        - "7. monthly_accumulated_cost += actual_cost"
        - "8. Log entry to cost-log.json"
    free_engines:
      - d2
      - mermaid
      - plotly
    paid_engines:
      - gpt_image
      - recraft
      - ideogram

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # CIRCUIT BREAKER (per API call retry logic)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  circuit_breaker:
    max_retries_per_call: 3
    description: >
      Maximum number of retry attempts for a single API call before aborting.
      After max_retries, the engine emits VisualError and visual-scout
      moves to the next engine in the fallback chain.
    behavior:
      on_retry: >
        Log retry attempt with: engine_id, attempt_number, error_type,
        timestamp. Respect engine-specific retry_delay_ms from visual-engines.yaml.
      on_max_reached: >
        Emit VisualError(type=engine_failure, message="circuit breaker tripped
        after ${max_retries} attempts"). Move to fallback_suggestion engine.
        Log circuit breaker event.
    retry_delay_strategy: use_engine_config
    notes: >
      Circuit breaker is per-call, not per-engine. Each new spec starts
      with a fresh retry counter. Engine-level retry_count from
      visual-engines.yaml takes precedence when it is lower than
      max_retries_per_call (e.g., gpt_image has retry_count=0, meaning
      no retries at all -- circuit breaker respects this).

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # COST LOG SCHEMA (cost-log.json)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  cost_log:
    file_path: "${SLIDES_DATA_DIR:-data}/cost-log.json"
    description: >
      Append-only log of every API call cost. Used for aggregation,
      reporting, and budget enforcement. Each entry is one render() call.
    entry_schema:
      id:
        type: string
        format: uuid_v4
        description: "Unique identifier for this log entry."
      timestamp:
        type: string
        format: iso_8601
        description: "When the API call was made."
      engine_id:
        type: string
        enum: [d2, mermaid, gpt_image, recraft, plotly, ideogram]
        description: "Which engine was called."
      cost_usd:
        type: number
        precision: 4
        description: "Actual cost incurred (0.0000 for free engines)."
      estimated_cost_usd:
        type: number
        precision: 4
        description: "Pre-call estimate from estimateCost()."
      deck_id:
        type: string
        description: "Deck identifier for per-deck aggregation."
      slide_index:
        type: number
        description: "Which slide in the deck triggered this call."
      content_type:
        type: string
        description: "Content type from VisualSpec (process, concept, etc.)."
      visual_type:
        type: string
        description: "Visual type from VisualSpec (flowchart, illustration, etc.)."
      cache_hit:
        type: boolean
        description: "True if result was served from cache (cost = 0)."
      success:
        type: boolean
        description: "True if render() succeeded, false if VisualError."
      error_type:
        type: string
        required: false
        description: "If success=false: engine_failure | brand_violation | timeout | budget_exceeded."
      retry_count:
        type: number
        description: "Number of retries before success or failure."
      generation_time_ms:
        type: number
        description: "Wall-clock time for this call in milliseconds."

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # AGGREGATION RULES
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  aggregation:
    description: >
      Cost log entries are aggregated at three granularities for reporting
      and budget enforcement. Aggregation is computed on-demand from
      cost-log.json, not stored separately.

    per_deck:
      group_by: deck_id
      metrics:
        - total_cost_usd: "SUM(cost_usd) WHERE deck_id = X"
        - total_calls: "COUNT(*) WHERE deck_id = X"
        - paid_calls: "COUNT(*) WHERE deck_id = X AND cost_usd > 0"
        - free_calls: "COUNT(*) WHERE deck_id = X AND cost_usd = 0"
        - cache_hits: "COUNT(*) WHERE deck_id = X AND cache_hit = true"
        - avg_cost_per_call: "AVG(cost_usd) WHERE deck_id = X AND cost_usd > 0"
      used_for: "Budget cap enforcement (SLIDES_COST_CAP)"

    per_day:
      group_by: "DATE(timestamp)"
      metrics:
        - total_cost_usd: "SUM(cost_usd) WHERE DATE(timestamp) = D"
        - total_calls: "COUNT(*) WHERE DATE(timestamp) = D"
        - unique_decks: "COUNT(DISTINCT deck_id) WHERE DATE(timestamp) = D"
      used_for: "Daily spend monitoring"

    per_month:
      group_by: "MONTH(timestamp)"
      metrics:
        - total_cost_usd: "SUM(cost_usd) WHERE MONTH(timestamp) = M"
        - total_calls: "COUNT(*) WHERE MONTH(timestamp) = M"
        - unique_decks: "COUNT(DISTINCT deck_id) WHERE MONTH(timestamp) = M"
        - budget_remaining_usd: "SLIDES_MONTHLY_BUDGET - SUM(cost_usd)"
        - budget_pct_used: "(SUM(cost_usd) / SLIDES_MONTHLY_BUDGET) * 100"
      used_for: "Monthly budget warning threshold (80%)"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # COST REFERENCE TABLE (from visual-engines.yaml)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  engine_costs:
    description: >
      Reference copy of per-call costs from visual-engines.yaml.
      Source of truth is visual-engines.yaml -- this section exists for
      quick lookup during cost tracking operations.
    engines:
      - id: d2
        cost_usd: 0.0000
        model: free_oss
      - id: mermaid
        cost_usd: 0.0000
        model: free_oss
      - id: gpt_image
        cost_usd: 0.0400
        model: gpt-image-1.5
      - id: recraft
        cost_usd: 0.0800
        model: recraft-v4
      - id: plotly
        cost_usd: 0.0000
        model: free_oss
      - id: ideogram
        cost_usd: 0.0400
        model: ideogram-v3

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # BUDGET SCENARIOS (for planning reference)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  budget_scenarios:
    description: >
      Pre-calculated scenarios showing how many images fit within budget caps.
      Used by slide-chief for planning and by visual-scout for engine selection.
    per_deck_2usd:
      gpt_image_only: "50 images ($0.04 each)"
      recraft_only: "25 images ($0.08 each)"
      ideogram_only: "50 images ($0.04 each)"
      mixed_typical: "20 GPT + 5 Recraft + unlimited diagrams = ~$1.20"
    per_month_100usd:
      decks_at_avg_1_20: "~83 decks/month"
      decks_at_max_2_00: "50 decks/month"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # INTEGRATION POINTS
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  integration:
    visual_scout:
      description: >
        visual-scout calls pre_call_check before every engine.render().
        On budget exceeded: skip paid engine, try free fallback.
      hook: "before_render"
      reads: [budget_caps, pre_call_check, cost_log]
      writes: [cost_log]

    slide_chief:
      description: >
        slide-chief reads cost aggregation after deck completion for
        reporting. Includes cost summary in deck delivery metadata.
      hook: "after_deck_complete"
      reads: [aggregation.per_deck, budget_scenarios]

    qa_inspector:
      description: >
        qa-inspector validates that deck cost is within budget cap
        as part of quality gate. Flags over-budget as a warning
        (not a killer item -- budget is enforced at generation time).
      hook: "quality_gate"
      reads: [aggregation.per_deck, budget_caps.per_deck]
```


## Referência: references/squad/data/design-direction.schema.yaml

```yaml
# Design Direction Schema — Slides Creator Squad
# Mission: MSN-2026-SLIDES-NARRATIVE-DESIGN (T-003B)
# Created: 2026-05-17
# Version: 1.0.0
#
# Schema for design-direction.yaml — emitted by tasks/define-design-direction.md
# Consumed by design-renderer, validate-visual-coherence, run-design-critique.
# Forces explicit design DIRECTION (not just brand skin) before any HTML/DeckSpec render.
#
# Closes GAP-010 (case-study Primeiro Servico de IA: identidade aplicada como skin).

meta:
  schema_version: "1.0.0"
  producer: "tasks/define-design-direction.md (T-015B)"
  consumers:
    - "tasks/compose-grid-layout.md"
    - "tasks/resolve-active-palette.md"
    - "tasks/run-design-critique.md (T-016)"
    - "tasks/validate-visual-coherence.md (T-009)"
  rubric_dim_ref: "data/qa-rubric.yaml#dimensions.design.sub_dimensions.visual_coherence"
  killer_items_enforced: [KI-10]

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SCHEMA
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
design_direction:
  required: [deck_id, visual_reference, dominant_motif, density_limits, variation_rules, composition_rules]
  fields:

    deck_id:
      type: string

    brand_ref:
      type: ["string", "null"]
      description: "Brandbook ou design-md path. Pode ser null para decks sem brand owner."

    visual_reference:
      type: object
      required: true
      description: >-
        Referência visual concreta (não é só brand tokens). Define o "deck-stage real".
      fields:
        type:
          type: enum
          values:
            - external_url           # ex: extracted via /design-md
            - prior_deck             # path para .pptx/.html de referência aprovada
            - mood_board             # paths de imagens (max 6)
            - design_system          # path para apps/{ds}/ component library
            - composite              # combinação dos acima
        paths:
          type: list
          item_type: string
          min_items: 1
        notes:
          type: string
          max_length: 280
          description: "O que especificamente extrair da referência (não 'copiar', mas 'inspirar-se em X')"

    dominant_motif:
      type: object
      required: true
      description: "O motif visual que se repete e dá unidade ao deck"
      fields:
        name:
          type: string
          example: "grid editorial estilo Pentagram"
        rationale:
          type: string
          max_length: 280
        rendered_as:
          type: list
          description: "Como o motif se manifesta (paddings, bordas, fundos, decorações)"
          item_type: string

    density_limits:
      type: object
      required: true
      description: "Limites de densidade por nível (consultado por validate-density)"
      fields:
        max_claims_governing_per_slide:
          type: integer
          default: 1
          min: 1
          max: 1
        max_claims_supporting_per_slide:
          type: integer
          default: 3
          min: 0
          max: 5
        max_visual_elements_per_slide:
          type: integer
          default: 4
          min: 1
          max: 7
        max_text_chars_per_slide:
          type: integer
          default: 280
          min: 50
          max: 600
        forbidden_patterns:
          type: list
          item_type: string
          examples:
            - "5+ cards iguais em grid (wireframe-like)"
            - "Bullet list > 5 itens"
            - "2+ charts na mesma slide"

    variation_rules:
      type: object
      required: true
      description: "Como o deck varia visualmente entre slides (evita monotonia tipo Primeiro Servico v1)"
      fields:
        layouts_count_min:
          type: integer
          default: 4
          description: "Mínimo de layouts distintos no deck"
        layout_repetition_max:
          type: integer
          default: 3
          description: "Mesmo layout pode aparecer no máximo X vezes consecutivas"
        quiet_slide_ratio_min:
          type: number
          default: 0.15
          description: "Pelo menos 15% dos slides devem ser quiet (1 claim minimal density)"
        accent_color_density:
          type: string
          enum: [sparse, moderate, dense]
          default: sparse
          description: "Distribuição de cor de destaque"
        motion_policy:
          type: enum
          values: [none, subtle_transitions, full_motion]
          default: subtle_transitions

    composition_rules:
      type: object
      required: true
      description: "Regras de composição enforced por compose-grid-layout"
      fields:
        grid_columns:
          type: integer
          default: 12
        baseline_padding_pt:
          type: integer
          default: 32
        title_anchor:
          type: enum
          values: [top_left, top_center, top_full]
          default: top_left
        footer_present:
          type: boolean
          default: true
        slide_number_visible:
          type: boolean
          default: true
        safe_area_pct:
          type: number
          default: 0.92
          description: "% do canvas para conteúdo (resto é margem técnica)"

    palette_constraints:
      type: object
      required: false
      description: "Constraints sobre active-palette resolution"
      fields:
        primary_anchor:
          type: string
          description: "Cor que ancora o deck (hex ou token ref)"
        accent_use:
          type: string
          enum: [single_per_slide, dual_per_slide, free]
          default: single_per_slide
        dark_mode:
          type: enum
          values: [light, dark, auto]
          default: light

    typography_constraints:
      type: object
      required: false
      fields:
        display_font_ref:
          type: string
          description: "Token ref (e.g., --slide-title-xl)"
        body_font_ref:
          type: string
        scale_steps:
          type: list
          item_type: string
          example: ["--slide-title-xl", "--slide-title-lg", "--slide-title-md", "--slide-body", "--slide-caption"]
        line_length_max_chars:
          type: integer
          default: 60

    audience_context:
      type: object
      required: true
      description: "Contexto da audiência que informa decisões visuais"
      fields:
        viewing_mode:
          type: enum
          values: [in_person_projection, webinar_screen, async_pdf, mobile_share]
          default: webinar_screen
        viewing_distance:
          type: string
          enum: [near, medium, far]
          default: medium
        audience_size:
          type: enum
          values: [intimate_under_20, medium_20_200, large_200_plus]
        attention_budget_minutes:
          type: integer
          default: 45

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# VALIDATION RULES
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
validation_rules:
  - rule: "visual_reference deve ter pelo menos 1 path real (não placeholder)"
    severity: blocking
    killer_item: KI-10
    rationale: "Identidade ≠ direção. Sem referência visual concreta, deck vira skin."

  - rule: "dominant_motif.name deve ser declarado (não vazio, não 'modern' / 'clean' / 'minimal')"
    severity: blocking
    rationale: "Buzzwords visuais são ausência de direção"

  - rule: "density_limits.max_claims_governing_per_slide == 1 (hard cap)"
    severity: blocking

  - rule: "variation_rules.layouts_count_min >= 4"
    severity: high
    rationale: "Deck monolayout = wireframe (lição Primeiro Servico v1)"

  - rule: "variation_rules.layout_repetition_max <= 3"
    severity: high
    case_study_ref: "Primeiro Servico v1: 5+ cards iguais consecutivos"

  - rule: "Se audience_context.viewing_mode = in_person_projection, contrast deve usar WCAG AAA (>=7:1)"
    severity: high

  - rule: "design_direction.yaml DEVE existir antes de qualquer render (HTML/TSX/PPTX)"
    severity: blocking
    killer_item: KI-10
    enforced_by: "tasks/handoff-render-request.md pre-condition"

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# EXAMPLE (derived from Primeiro Servico de IA v3 retrospective)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
example:
  deck_id: "primeiro-servico-ia-v3"
  brand_ref: "workspace/businesses/aiox/L2-tactical/brand/"

  visual_reference:
    type: composite
    paths:
      - "workspace/businesses/aiox/L2-tactical/design/reference-decks/y-combinator-demo-day-2024.pdf"
      - "outputs/webinars/primeiro-servico-ia/draft-slides-aiox-v3-key.html"
    notes: "Editorial workshop vibe — Pentagram-esque, blocos de cor sólida, tipografia condensada protagonista. NÃO copiar layouts; adotar disciplina."

  dominant_motif:
    name: "Bloco de cor sólida como cenário do título"
    rationale: "Cria âncora visual recorrente sem virar wireframe. Cada slide-chave tem 'cortina' de cor."
    rendered_as:
      - "Block fundo lime/dark cobrindo 30-50% do canvas"
      - "Tipografia black/extrabold sobre o bloco"
      - "Espaço branco respiratório no restante"

  density_limits:
    max_claims_governing_per_slide: 1
    max_claims_supporting_per_slide: 3
    max_visual_elements_per_slide: 4
    max_text_chars_per_slide: 240
    forbidden_patterns:
      - "5+ cards iguais em grid"
      - "Matriz com mais de 12 células visíveis simultaneamente"
      - "Bullet list > 5 itens"

  variation_rules:
    layouts_count_min: 6
    layout_repetition_max: 2
    quiet_slide_ratio_min: 0.2
    accent_color_density: sparse
    motion_policy: subtle_transitions

  composition_rules:
    grid_columns: 12
    baseline_padding_pt: 48
    title_anchor: top_left
    footer_present: true
    slide_number_visible: true
    safe_area_pct: 0.9

  palette_constraints:
    primary_anchor: "--bb-lime"
    accent_use: single_per_slide
    dark_mode: light

  typography_constraints:
    display_font_ref: "--slide-title-xl"
    body_font_ref: "--slide-body"
    scale_steps:
      - "--slide-title-xl"
      - "--slide-title-lg"
      - "--slide-title-md"
      - "--slide-body"
      - "--slide-caption"
    line_length_max_chars: 50

  audience_context:
    viewing_mode: webinar_screen
    viewing_distance: medium
    audience_size: medium_20_200
    attention_budget_minutes: 60

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ANTI-PATTERNS
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
anti_patterns:
  - name: "Brand-as-skin"
    description: "Apenas brand tokens (cores+fonts+logo) declarados, sem visual_reference real"
    detection: "visual_reference.paths == [] OR vazio"
    killer_item: KI-10
    case_study_ref: "Primeiro Servico de IA v1"

  - name: "Buzzword direction"
    description: "dominant_motif.name é 'modern', 'clean', 'minimal', 'professional'"
    detection: "regex match"
    severity: blocking

  - name: "Monolayout"
    description: "layouts_count_min < 4 OR 1 layout repete em >50% dos slides"
    severity: high

  - name: "No audience context"
    description: "audience_context vazio"
    severity: blocking
    rationale: "Decisões visuais sem contexto de audiência são chute"
```


## Referência: references/squad/data/design-philosophies.md

# Design Philosophies — Taxonomy para Decks Sinkra

> **Purpose:** taxonomia de 20 filosofias de design em 5 escolas, usada como fallback quando brief é visualmente vago e não há design context existente (brand spec, UI kit, reference).
> **Consumer:** `slide-chief` (routing) + `tasks/advise-design-direction.md` (quando implementado) + `design-renderer` (prompt composition).
> **Scope:** aplicável a qualquer deck output (slide HTML, PDF, PPTX). Escola e filosofia escolhidas influenciam typography, color palette, layout density, motion intensity.

---

## Princípio de uso

Esta taxonomia é **fallback**, não default. Ordem de precedência para resolver visual style:

1. **Brand spec existente** — se business tem brandbook/UI kit no workspace, respeitar integralmente
2. **Reference fornecido pelo user** — screenshot, link, product that inspires
3. **Existing design system (shadcn/ui + tokens)** — se deck é para produto que já tem DS, seguir
4. **Esta taxonomia** — só se 1-3 falham e user pede "sugestões de estilo"

**Regra de diferenciação:** quando recomendar 3 filosofias ao user como opções, elas DEVEM vir de **3 escolas distintas** — evitar pitch de 3 minimalismos levemente diferentes.

---

## As 5 escolas

| Escola | Princípio central | Quando escolher | Ideal para sinkra business |
|---|---|---|---|
| Information Architecture | "Dados não são decoração, são material de construção" | Audience sophisticated, data-heavy narrative | AIOX institucional, Bilhon investor deck |
| Motion Poetics | "Tecnologia tem ritmo" | Launch, product demo, brand video | AIOX launch, Academia Lendária promos |
| Minimalism | "Reduzir até não dar mais" | Premium, editorial, pitch alto-ticket | AllFluence luxo, executive deck |
| Experimental Avant-garde | "Quebrar regras cria regras" | Creative industries, cultural cover | Academia Lendária cover, creative campaigns |
| Eastern Philosophy | "Vazio é conteúdo" | Reflective, thoughtful, artisan | AllFluence premium, brand manifesto |

---

## Filosofia-por-filosofia

### Escola 1 — Information Architecture

#### 1.1 — Editorial Typography (Pentagram lineage)

**Princípio:** tipografia é a linguagem principal. Grid matemática é o esqueleto.

**Características visuais:**
- Preto + branco + 1 accent color (máx)
- Grid Swiss com spacing matemático preciso (8pt ou 4pt baseline)
- Type hierarchy extrema (título 10× body)
- Negative space estratégico (60%+ whitespace)
- Zero decoração, tudo serve conteúdo

**Quando usar:** executive summary, strategy deck, research report, corporate narrative.

**Prompt DNA:**
```
Editorial typography grade. Strict grid (8pt baseline). Display typography
as primary visual language. Two-color palette: ink black + single accent.
60%+ whitespace. Type hierarchy extreme (48pt titles over 16pt body).
No decoration. Data viz uses same type language as body text.
```

#### 1.2 — Scientific Data Visualization (Fathom lineage)

**Princípio:** cada pixel carrega informação. Rigor acadêmico com polish de design.

**Características visuais:**
- Palette neutra (grays, navy, 1 highlight color)
- Sans-serif racional (Graphik, GT America, ou Inter com ajuste)
- Charts precisos com axis labels, footnotes, attribution
- Citations integradas ao layout (não afterthought)
- Alta densidade de informação sem clutter

**Quando usar:** data-intensive deck, annual report, research whitepaper, financial analysis.

**Prompt DNA:**
```
Scientific journal meets modern design. Precision data visualization
(charts, timelines, scatter plots). Neutral scheme (grays, navy, one
highlight). Clean rationalist sans-serif. Citation and footnote design
integrated. High information density without clutter.
```

#### 1.3 — Content-First Reading (iA lineage)

**Princípio:** design é invisível. Conteúdo é a única coisa que importa.

**Características visuais:**
- System fonts apenas (SF Pro, Roboto, Inter)
- Blue classical hyperlinks (#0000EE ou variant)
- Reading-optimized line length (66 characters max)
- Progressive disclosure (headlines + collapsible detail)
- Zero visual decoration

**Quando usar:** long-form essay, policy paper, manifesto, quarterly letter.

**Prompt DNA:**
```
Content-first, zero decorative elements. System fonts only. Classic blue
hyperlinks. Reading line length 66 chars. Progressive disclosure layout.
Text-heavy, fast-loading aesthetic. Design disappears to serve text.
```

#### 1.4 — Cartographic Information (Stamen lineage)

**Princípio:** deixar dados se tornarem paisagem tocável.

**Características visuais:**
- Palette quente de dataviz (terracotta, sage, deep blue)
- Padrões algorítmicos/orgânicos
- Camadas de informação como mapa topográfico
- Sensação hand-crafted apesar da precisão digital
- Soft shadows e depth

**Quando usar:** geographic data, network analysis, flow visualization, ecosystem map.

**Prompt DNA:**
```
Cartographic approach to data visualization. Organic, algorithm-generated
patterns. Warm palette (terracotta, sage green, deep blues). Layered
information like topographic maps. Hand-crafted feel. Soft shadows.
```

---

### Escola 2 — Motion Poetics

#### 2.1 — Cinematic Scroll (Locomotive lineage)

**Princípio:** scroll não é navegação, é jornada.

**Características visuais:**
- Parallax depth + motion blur
- Generous vertical spacing
- Dark mode base com strategic glow accents
- Hero sections 100vh
- Film-like scene composition

**Quando usar:** launch site, product announcement, immersive story deck.

**Prompt DNA:**
```
Film-like scene composition with parallax depth. Generous vertical spacing.
Bold typography emerging from darkness. Smooth motion blur. Dark base
with strategic glowing accents. 100vh hero sections.
```

#### 2.2 — WebGL Particles (Active Theory lineage)

**Princípio:** tornar a tecnologia visível = tornar compreensível.

**Características visuais:**
- Sistemas de partículas 3D
- Neon gradients (cyan/magenta/electric blue) on dark
- Mouse-reactive environments
- Depth of field + bokeh
- Glassmorphism com moderação

**Quando usar:** AI product launch, tech demonstration, interactive experience.

**Prompt DNA:**
```
Particle systems representing data flow. 3D visualization in depth space.
Neon gradients (cyan, magenta, electric blue) on dark. Mouse-reactive
environment. Depth of field. Floating UI with measured glassmorphism.
```

#### 2.3 — Algorithmic Generative (Field.io lineage)

**Princípio:** código é o designer.

**Características visuais:**
- Padrões geométricos gerados por algoritmo
- Base monocromática + accent vibrante
- Precisão matemática no spacing
- Voronoi / Delaunay patterns
- Estética de clean code

**Quando usar:** tech brand foundation, generative art cover, computational design.

**Prompt DNA:**
```
Abstract geometric patterns, algorithmically generated. Dynamic
composition feeling computational. Monochromatic base with vibrant
accent. Mathematical precision. Voronoi or Delaunay patterns.
```

#### 2.4 — Narrative Interaction (Resn lineage)

**Princípio:** cada click avança a história.

**Características visuais:**
- Illustrative style + UI elements
- Gamified exploration (progress indicators)
- Warm palette apesar do subject tech
- Character-driven design
- Scroll-triggered reveals

**Quando usar:** education product, course launch, journey-style storytelling.

**Prompt DNA:**
```
Illustrative style mixed with UI. Gamified exploration with progress
indicators. Warm color palette. Character-driven design. Scroll-triggered
animations. Editorial illustration meets product design.
```

---

### Escola 3 — Minimalism

#### 3.1 — Conceptual Monochrome (Experimental Jetset lineage)

**Princípio:** uma ideia = uma forma.

**Características visuais:**
- Primary colors only (red/blue/yellow) + black/white
- Typography como gráfico principal
- Single visual metaphor pro deck inteiro
- Grid-based com deliberate rule-breaking
- Anti-commercial aesthetic

**Quando usar:** cultural deck, exhibition catalog, manifesto, brand identity pitch.

#### 3.2 — Swiss Grid Purity (Müller-Brockmann lineage)

**Princípio:** objetividade é beleza.

**Características visuais:**
- Grid matemático rigoroso (8pt baseline)
- Alinhamento estrito (flush left ou centered)
- Máximo 2 cores (preto + 1 accent)
- Akzidenz-Grotesk ou sans racional similar
- Zero ornamento

**Quando usar:** foundational brand work, timeless archival, high-culture institution.

#### 3.3 — Premium Restraint (Build lineage)

**Princípio:** simples polido é mais difícil que complexo.

**Características visuais:**
- Whitespace generoso (70%+ da área)
- Weight shifts sutis (200 → 600)
- Single accent color usada com parcimônia
- High-end photography aesthetic
- Golden ratio proportions

**Quando usar:** luxury brand, premium pricing pitch, high-ticket service, executive communication.

#### 3.4 — Joyful Minimalism (Sagmeister & Walsh lineage)

**Princípio:** beleza é função com emoção.

**Características visuais:**
- Unexpected color bursts em base minimal
- Handmade elements em digital
- Optimistic visual language
- Experimental typography que mantém legibilidade
- Warmth through deliberate imperfection

**Quando usar:** people-focused brand, mission-driven org, human service deck.

---

### Escola 4 — Experimental Avant-garde

#### 4.1 — Code as Drawing (Lieberman lineage)

**Princípio:** programar é pintar.

**Características visuais:**
- Hand-drawn feel gerado por código
- Preto e branco puros
- Real-time generative patterns
- Sketch-like line quality
- Visible process / grid / construction lines

**Quando usar:** creative tech showcase, coding education, art-code crossover.

#### 4.2 — Parametric Architecture (Kwok lineage)

**Princípio:** beleza do sistema supera beleza do indivíduo.

**Características visuais:**
- Fractal patterns, recursive structures
- High-contrast black and white
- Architectural visualization of data
- Intricate detail rewarding zoom
- Processing / creative coding aesthetic

**Quando usar:** architectural practice, computational design firm, technical depth pitch.

#### 4.3 — Cyber Poetics (Thorp lineage)

**Princípio:** o futuro não é frio, é solitário poético.

**Características visuais:**
- Film-grade lighting
- Warm cyberpunk (orange/teal, NOT cold blue)
- Industrial design meets luxury
- Narrative concept art feel
- Volumetric lighting, god rays

**Quando usar:** film/gaming brand, cyberpunk-adjacent product, cinematic narrative deck.

#### 4.4 — FUI / Fantasy Interface (Territory lineage)

**Princípio:** imaginar UI do futuro hoje.

**Características visuais:**
- Holographic projection aesthetics
- Orange/amber monochrome OR cyan accents
- Multiple overlapping data layers
- Believable future technology
- Technical readouts, data streams

**Quando usar:** sci-fi content, speculative design, experiential tech demo.

---

### Escola 5 — Eastern Philosophy

#### 5.1 — Speculative Design (Takram lineage)

**Princípio:** tecnologia é meio de pensamento.

**Características visuais:**
- Concept prototypes elegantes
- Soft tech aesthetic (rounded corners, gentle shadows)
- Charts como peças de arte
- Neutral natural colors (beige, soft gray, muted green)
- Modest sophistication

**Quando usar:** research-driven product, thoughtful consultancy pitch, strategic foresight deck.

#### 5.2 — Emptiness Design (Kenya Hara lineage)

**Princípio:** design não é preencher, é esvaziar.

**Características visuais:**
- Whitespace extremo (80%+)
- Paper texture em digital
- Camadas de branco (warm white, cool white, off-white)
- Minimal color, se houver muito desaturated
- Zen simplicity

**Quando usar:** museum exhibit, luxury minimalist brand, meditation-adjacent product, art book.

#### 5.3 — Book Architecture (Boom lineage)

**Princípio:** informação tem poética física.

**Características visuais:**
- Non-linear information structure
- Play with edges, margins, boundaries
- Unexpected color combos (pink+red, orange+brown)
- Handcraft translated to digital
- Dense information inviting exploration
- Editorial, unconventional grid

**Quando usar:** annual report art edition, catalog, dense storytelling, archive piece.

#### 5.4 — Ink Wash Digital (Eastern modernist lineage)

**Princípio:** tecnologia precisa de temperatura humana.

**Características visuais:**
- Digital interpretation of ink wash painting
- Soft glow, light diffusion
- Poetic negative space
- Emotional palette (deep blues, warm grays, soft gold)
- Calligraphic influences in typography

**Quando usar:** Asian market, cultural-tech crossover, meditative brand, artisan product.

---

## Prompt composition

Quando filosofia é aplicada a um slide/deck, prompt para AI image generation combina:

```
[Philosophy prompt DNA] + [Scene context] + [Specific content/subject]
```

**Princípio crítico (aprendido do espaço):**
> **Describe mood, not layout.** AI image generation responde melhor a
> 3 frases de emoção do que a 30 linhas de layout specification.

**Good prompt example:**
```
Data visualization with Editorial Typography feel — Bloomberg
Businessweek aesthetic. Key number "45%" dominates the composition
like a magazine headline. Warm cream tones, sharp black typography.
Data tells story of market shift.
```

**Bad prompt example (over-constrained, AI produces empty output):**
```
Professional slide. Navy 60%, white 30%, gold 10%. Title centered 36pt
Helvetica. Two columns below. Left: bullets 18pt. Right: bar chart.
Margins: 40px all sides. Grid 8pt baseline. [...]
```

---

## Workflow integration

### Task trigger: `tasks/advise-design-direction.md` (a ser criado)

Invoked quando:
- `briefing.design_context.status == "absent"`
- AND `briefing.reference_material is None`
- AND user prompted "quero sugestões de estilo" / "não sei o visual"

### Output esperado

User receives 3 filosofias (de 3 escolas diferentes) com:
- Nome da filosofia
- 50-100 palavras explicando por que é fit para este brief específico
- 3-4 características visuais centrais
- 3-5 keywords de mood
- Opcional: 1 obra de referência citada

Plus 3 visual demos (gerados em paralelo quando possível) como thumbnails para escolha rápida.

## Referência: references/squad/data/edge-case-decisions.yaml

```yaml
# Edge Case Decision Registry — slides-creator
# Extracted from McKinsey PPT Architect "TROUBLESHOOTING & EDGE CASES"
# Consumed by: slide-chief routing + D01/D02/D03 gate advisors + normalize-briefing

schema_version: "1.0"
name: edge-case-decisions
owner_squad: slides-creator
source: "docs/squad/slides/enterprise_slides/output/mckinsey_ppt_architect_instructions.md#TROUBLESHOOTING"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# DECISION REGISTRY (indexed by symptom)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
edge_cases:

  - id: EC-01
    symptom: "Material fonte é ambíguo ou contraditório"
    detected_by: [catalog-sources-apa, p1-fidelity-sampling]
    resolution_protocol:
      - step: "NUNCA resolver ambiguidade inventando dados (P1 Fidelidade violation)"
      - step: "Documentar explicitamente no slide com marker VALIDAR COM CLIENTE"
      - step: "Sinalizar em vermelho/destaque para revisão obrigatória"
      - step: "Se crítico para narrativa, pausar e perguntar ao cliente antes de continuar"
    marker_template: |
      [VALIDAR COM CLIENTE: Fonte A menciona X, Fonte B menciona Y.
      Utilizamos X (Fonte A) por ser mais recente, mas requer confirmação.]
    escalation: D01_gate (narrative approval)
    owner: content-architect

  - id: EC-02
    symptom: "Dados insuficientes para preencher slide planejado"
    detected_by: [catalog-sources-apa, build-pyramid]
    resolution_protocol:
      - step: "NÃO inventar dados placeholder (P1 violation)"
      - step: "Documentar gap explicitamente com marker"
      - step: "Oferecer 3 opções ao cliente"
    options:
      A: "Reduzir escopo do slide (ex: só regiões com dados)"
      B: "Cliente fornece dados faltantes"
      C: "Eliminar slide se não essencial"
    marker_template: |
      [SLIDE PLANEJADO: {descrição}]
      [DADOS DISPONÍVEIS: {o que tem}]
      [DADOS FALTANTES: {o que falta}]
      [OPÇÕES: A) {reduce} B) {fill} C) {eliminate}]
      [AGUARDANDO DECISÃO DO CLIENTE]
    escalation: D01_gate OR D02_gate depending on phase
    owner: slide-chief

  - id: EC-03
    symptom: "Número de slides excede target do cliente"
    detected_by: [classify-slide-type, build-pyramid]
    resolution_protocol:
      - step: "NÃO comprimir informação com perda de clareza"
      - step: "Apresentar 3 opções ao cliente"
    options:
      A: "Manter slides, apresentação será X min (vs Y desejado)"
      B: "Mover slides para Appendix (conteúdo disponível mas não apresentado)"
      C: "Eliminar seção (explicar impacto na narrativa)"
    recommendation_priority: "Baseado em prioridade de mensagens na pyramid"
    escalation: D02_gate (structure approval)
    owner: content-architect

  - id: EC-04
    symptom: "Brand guidelines do cliente conflitam com best practices"
    detected_by: [detect-brand-override, compose-grid-layout]
    resolution_protocol:
      - step: "Seguir brand guidelines (cliente > best practices)"
      - step: "Documentar trade-off explicitamente"
      - step: "Sugerir alternativas diplomaticamente se houver problemas sérios (ex: contraste WCAG insuficiente)"
    marker_template: |
      [NOTA: Brand guidelines especificam {X}, que não é recomendado para
      apresentações executivas. Seguindo guidelines do cliente mas sinalizando
      para discussão se necessário.]
    escalation: D03_gate + STK-10 co-sign
    owner: visual-scout
    hard_stop_conditions:
      - "Contraste WCAG AA falha (< 4.5:1) — sinalizar como bloqueador independente"

  - id: EC-05
    symptom: "Cliente pede slide de impacto mas dados são negativos"
    detected_by: [build-pyramid, write-action-titles]
    resolution_protocol:
      - step: "NUNCA manipular dados para parecerem melhores (P1 violation)"
      - step: "Tentar reframing honesto (magnitude, trend, ratio, comparison)"
      - step: "Se não houver reframing honesto possível, apresentar dado negativo com action plan"
    reframing_examples:
      bad: "Receita caiu 30%"
      good_option_a: "Receita ainda caiu, mas ritmo de declínio desacelerou em 50%"
      bad_2: "Perdemos 5 clientes top"
      good_option_b: "Retivemos 82% da base de clientes enterprise apesar de pressão competitiva"
      when_no_reframing_works:
        title: "Receita caiu 30% em 2024, exigindo plano de turnaround urgente"
        content: "Dado + Causas raiz + Próximas ações"
    escalation: D01_gate
    owner: content-architect

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# GENERAL ESCALATION LADDER (applies to any detected edge case)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
escalation_ladder:
  tier_0: "Agent resolves via protocol (no human needed)"
  tier_1: "slide-chief review + decision"
  tier_2: "D01/D02/D03 gate (human operator)"
  tier_3: "STK-10 co-sign (brand/strategic)"
  tier_4: "HALT pipeline — await client input"

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CONSUMER INTEGRATION
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
integration:
  slide_chief:
    action: "Consult this registry before routing any work blocked by data ambiguity"
  d01_gate:
    action: "Check if any EC-* markers present in pyramid-tree or sources-apa; surface to Human"
  d02_gate:
    action: "Check for EC-03 (slide count) before approving structure"
  d03_gate:
    action: "Check for EC-04 (brand conflict) before approving design; trigger STK-10 if needed"
  normalize_briefing:
    action: "Pre-detect EC-02 by flagging missing data points in input"

meta:
  absorbed_from: "mckinsey_ppt_architect_instructions.md lines 1489-1553"
  absorbed_date: "2026-04-21"
  total_cases: 5
```


## Referência: references/squad/data/editable-vs-image-pptx-decision.md

# Editable vs Image PPTX — Decision Matrix

> **Purpose:** decidir qual modo de export PPTX usar quando `delivery_format` inclui C
> **Consumers:** `design-renderer`, `qa-inspector`, `slide-chief` (release gate)

---

## The two modes

### Editable mode

- **Como:** DOM lido elemento por elemento → objetos PowerPoint nativos (text frame / shape / picture)
- **Resultado:** cliente abre PPTX, duplo-clique em um texto, edita palavras
- **Restrição:** HTML precisa seguir 4 hard constraints desde a primeira linha (ver `tasks/export-editable-pptx.md`)
- **Visual fidelity:** ~70% (font fallback possível no destino; alguns features CSS não mapeiam)

### Image mode

- **Como:** cada slide HTML é screenshot via Playwright em PNG 1920×1080 → PNG inserido como full-slide image em pptxgenjs
- **Resultado:** visual 100% idêntico ao browser. Mas cliente não consegue editar texto.
- **Restrição:** nenhuma (HTML pode ter qualquer CSS)
- **Visual fidelity:** 100%

---

## Decision matrix

| Critério | Editable | Image |
|---|---|---|
| Cliente vai editar texto após entrega | ✅ | ❌ |
| Apresentação única, arquivado depois | ❌ | ✅ |
| Visual tem gradients complexos / web component / SVG avançado | ❌ (não suporta) | ✅ |
| Visual tem CSS simples (solid colors, basic layout) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Font stack não está no Office do destino | ⚠️ fallback | ✅ (raster preserva) |
| Precisa visual 100% pixel-perfect | ⚠️ ~70% | ✅ 100% |
| Precisa de texto pesquisável no PowerPoint | ✅ | ❌ (texto é pixel) |
| Precisa de text-to-speech / accessibility reader no PPTX | ✅ | ❌ |
| Tamanho de arquivo | 📄 Menor (XML + assets) | 📦 Maior (17 PNGs embutidos) |
| Manter deck ao longo do tempo (revisões) | ✅ (editar direto) | ❌ (reeditar HTML, reexport) |

---

## Decision flow

```
Cliente precisa editar texto após entrega? ─────┐
│                                                │
├── SIM                                          │
│   └── HTML já segue 4 constraints?             │
│       ├── SIM → **Editable mode**              │
│       └── NÃO → Retornar erro, reescrever HTML │
│                  OU aceitar image mode com     │
│                  caveat explícito              │
│                                                │
└── NÃO / NÃO SEI                                │
    └── Visual pede CSS complexo (gradient,      │
        web component, complex SVG)?             │
        ├── SIM → **Image mode**                 │
        └── NÃO → **Editable mode** (mais        │
                   robusto long-term)            │
```

---

## When Editable is worth the constraint discipline

Adotar editable mode + seguir as 4 constraints vale a pena quando:

1. **Deck é long-lived** — vai ser editado/revisado ao longo de meses
2. **Multiple authors** — colegas não-técnicos vão ajustar copy
3. **Content-focused, visual-simple** — cards, números, texto, charts vetoriais
4. **Template brand-governed** — CSS é limitado, constraints não doem
5. **Accessibility matters** — screen readers precisam de texto real
6. **Localization** — traduções exigem edit direto no PPTX

---

## When Image mode is the pragmatic choice

Adotar image mode quando:

1. **Deck é one-shot** — apresenta uma vez, arquiva
2. **Single author** — quem fez quem reedita (HTML-first workflow)
3. **Visual-heavy** — gradientes, glassmorphism, web components críticos
4. **Visual fidelity é dealbreaker** — 70% de fidelity não é aceitável pro cliente
5. **HTML já existe livre** — não tem budget pra reescrever seguindo 4 constraints
6. **Design-system custom** — visuals que editable não consegue traduzir

---

## Hybrid strategy (per-slide mode)

Caso real: deck de 20 páginas, sendo 5 "heavy visual" (capa, section dividers, infographic) e 15 "content-focused" (data, bullets, frameworks).

Pode-se exportar **híbrido**:
- Slides 1, 5, 10, 15, 20 (heavy) → image mode
- Slides 2-4, 6-9, 11-14, 16-19 (content) → editable mode
- Merge em pptxgenjs single deck

Trade-off: PPTX final tem ~75% dos slides editáveis + os 5 heavies em imagem. Compromise aceitável se cliente precisa editar conteúdo mas não disputa o visual dos dividers.

---

## Handoff note pro cliente

Quando entregar deck em **image mode**, incluir em delivery note:

```
⚠️ Este deck está em modo image — textos são renderizados como imagem
para preservar fidelidade visual. Para edições de conteúdo:

1. Edições pequenas (palavra, correção typo): nos retorne o ticket, refazemos
2. Edições grandes (reescrita section): forneça o novo texto, atualizamos HTML+PPTX
3. Se você precisa editar diretamente no PowerPoint no futuro, podemos migrar
   para modo editable em um sprint dedicado (ver constraints em export-editable-pptx).
```

Quando entregar **editable mode**, nenhuma nota extra — cliente edita como qualquer PPTX.

---

## Related

- `tasks/confirm-delivery-format.md` — onde decisão começa
- `tasks/export-editable-pptx.md` — implementação editable
- `data/render-modes.yaml` — config técnica dos modos
